problem_statement: When determining which flash partition holds the running application, the system only checks whether the partition's offset range overlaps the load offset. This can produce a false result if a partition on a different flash controller (e.g. external memory) happens to have a matching offset range. The determination must also verify that the partition resides on the same flash controller (MTD device) as the code partition, so that only partitions on the correct controller are considered the running application partition.

problem_statement_fixed:
When determining which flash partition holds the running application, the system only checks whether the partition's offset range overlaps the load offset. This can produce a false result if a partition on a different flash controller (e.g. external memory) happens to have a matching offset range. The determination must also verify that the partition resides on the same flash controller (MTD device) as the code partition, so that only partitions on the correct controller are considered the running application partition.

To support this, the fixed-partition public interface in zephyr/storage/flash_map.h must provide two macros: FIXED_PARTITION_MTD(label), which takes a partition node label and returns the DTS node identifier of the MTD device/flash controller on which that partition resides, and FIXED_PARTITION_NODE_MTD(node), which takes a partition node identifier and returns the corresponding MTD device node identifier. Both macros must yield the correct MTD node for both regular fixed partitions and fixed subpartitions. The running-application partition check must compare these MTD device node identifiers in addition to the existing offset-range overlap check.
